pairs.why: A keeps a mid-key pink-violet sky with a clear lighter glow behind the sails and mid-value teal water like the real card, while B's deep saturated magenta corners and dark blue water push the contrast harder.
Both put a bright cyan top-left against dark navy lower-right, which is brighter and more contrasty than the real card's darker, even teal-navy field, so my vector gives no reason to choose.
B's darker ivy-and-arch frame with shaded corners and a central blue door matches the real card's dark vignette, while A's pale wall, lantern glow and bright pot raise the overall key.
A's green is deeper and its glow behind the duck is milder, closer to the real card's mid-dark green with a soft light centre, while B's lime halo is brighter and blows out more.
B is slightly lighter and airier with a softer city background, closer to the real card's high key, while A has a heavier grey floor and darker mass.
B has gentler contrast and a more muted mid-value sea, closer to the real card, though the real card's glow near the hull is also in A.
Both are bright, high-key, flat blue-sky scenes, while the real card is a darker, richer, tighter-value composition, so neither is closer.
A's lighter lavender-violet ring field is nearer the real card's mid-light flat purple, while B darkens toward the corners with a stronger vignette.
